title: Technology that blocks DGA domains | Kaspersky official blog
description: This content describes a technology used by Kaspersky to detect and block email spam domains generated by domain generation algorithms (DGAs). Spammers use DGAs to create many similar domain names automatically, making it difficult to block spam by individual domain names. Kaspersky's solution clusters similar domains and creates rules to block entire batches of these generated domains, improving spam filtering efficiency. The technology is part of Kaspersky's corporate email security solutions and helps reduce spam, phishing, and malware emails.
aiSummary: Kaspersky employs a technology that detects domains generated by domain generation algorithms (DGAs), which spammers use to register large numbers of similar domains automatically. When an email is flagged as spam, its domain is analyzed and, if meeting certain criteria, added to a database of 'bad' domains. A cascade of classifiers groups similar domains into clusters and generates concise blocking rules that cover entire clusters of DGA-generated domains. These rules are distributed to Kaspersky's email protection solutions, enabling them to block emails from these domains, even if the domains have not yet been used in spam campaigns. This approach allows efficient bulk blocking of spam domains and reduces the impact of spam, phishing, and malware emails on corporate customers.
aiImpact: The technology reduces the volume of spam, phishing, and malware emails reaching users by blocking entire clusters of DGA-generated domains with a single rule. This decreases employee distraction, wasted time, and exposure to malicious content delivered via email. It improves the effectiveness of email security solutions by addressing the challenge posed by the automated, large-scale registration of similar spam domains.
